feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $R$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QR}=\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PM}+\overset{\to }{MT}+\overset{\to }{TR}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/c42a0b8323c282a573244591d900801194f2f5b7382aabe60dedd903b896a029.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QP}=b,\,\overset{\to }{PM}=-c,\,\overset{\to }{MT}=d,\,\overset{\to }{TR}=a.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/9876c3c4947aa9d61e687138bfb6fb26040e7c334af8b02914f5857ae1616e98.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QR} & =\overset{\to }{QP}+\overset{\to }{PM}+\overset{\to }{MT}+\overset{\to }{TR} \\  & =b-c+d+a.\end{aligned}
$$
